policy.expiry: A decision is scoped to the content digest of the family its case belongs to, not the whole corpus. Adding an unrelated family must not expire every decision -- the evidence ledger learned that the hard way when the aaa and native families expired all 72 of its records at once.
policy.sourcing: Every decision cites a public source. An assertion is never changed to match current tool behaviour alone; that would make the corpus track the tools instead of the standard.
policy.scope: An assertion no engine reports is not thereby wrong, and not thereby right. Two engines agreeing on silence is enough to flag a question, never enough to settle it as wrong.

A sticky bar covers the focused control. The defect exists only while a control has focus, so it needs a focus walk and a geometry comparison. A single page load never enters that state.

decisions.rationale: Generic link text with no disambiguating context. Detecting a fixed set of generic phrases is mechanical and no engine consulted does it; judging whether the surrounding context resolves the purpose is not.

The inputs collect a name and an email and carry no autocomplete token, which is what the criterion requires. Engines check that an autocomplete value is valid, not that one is present, because deciding an input collects information about the user needs an understanding of the form.
Whether a heading or label describes its topic is a judgement about the content and its audience. No parse decides it, and an engine that tried would be guessing.
The contrast failure appears only under a dark colour scheme. Every engine ran under the default light scheme, so the failing rendering was never produced.
decisions.notes: Re-pinned in a contributor pull request for #55 after the page was redesigned. The rationale was previously stronger than the page: the old fixture had no dark-scheme stylesheet, so no dark rendering existed to be driven. The email now declares light and dark support and its prefers-color-scheme: dark rule leaves #333 text on #121212 (1.48:1), so the failure does appear only under a dark colour scheme, as this decision says. The assertion (1.4.3) is unchanged; the re-pin awaits maintainer confirmation.

The broken page carried an image with no alternative that its control had, unrelated to the EPUB package metadata the pair declares. Every engine detected it and nothing on the control, so the pair measured the wrong thing.
undeclared_findings.remedy: Give the broken page the same alternative text as its control so the pair differs only in package metadata and heading structure. Applied in #49; this baseline predates the fix. Verified applied: the broken page now carries the same alternative as its control, and axe reports nothing on either.
